title: Pitru rina: a debt carried towards the ancestors

text.en: The Sun, the 9th house or its lord stands with Rahu or Ketu. Tamil and Kerala practice reads this as pitru rina: something left unsettled on the father's and the forefathers' side.
text.impact: In this life it tends to show as a father who was absent, unwell or preoccupied; as family property or family matters that never quite resolve; or as a sense of carrying something for people who came before you. What settles it is observance rather than worry: tarpanam on the new-moon day and during Mahalaya paksha, and looking after the elders who are still here.

title: Matru rina: a debt carried towards the mother

text.en: The Moon or the 4th house stands with Rahu or Ketu, which Tamil practice reads as matru rina: something unsettled on the mother's side.
text.impact: It tends to show as a mother who carried more than her share, as distance or difficulty in that bond, or as a home that never felt entirely settled. What settles it is plain: care given to your mother now, or to elder women who stand in that place, and worship of Ambal on Mondays.

title: Sarpa shapa: the serpent debt, read on the house of children

text.en: Rahu or Ketu occupies the 5th house. Kerala practice especially reads this as sarpa shapa, the serpent debt, carried into the house of progeny and merit.
text.impact: It is read as delay or difficulty in matters of children, and sometimes as a pull towards the sacred that was interrupted. The customary answer is the naga worship and the Ayilyam puja listed below; medical help, where it is needed, is no quarrel of the tradition's.

title: Guru shapa: a debt carried towards teachers
subject: jupiter

text.en: Jupiter, the karaka of teachers and of dharma, stands with Rahu or Ketu. The tradition reads this as guru shapa: instruction taken and not honoured, or guidance left unfinished.
text.impact: It tends to show as teachers who disappoint, advice that misleads, or study begun and set down. What settles it is to become reliable in the role yourself: keep your word to those who teach you, finish what you begin, and teach freely where you can.

title: Patni shapa: a debt carried in marriage
subject: venus

text.en: Venus or the lord of the 7th stands with Rahu or Ketu, which the tradition reads as a bond from before that was left in difficulty.
text.impact: It tends to show as a marriage that asks unusual patience early on, or as a partner who arrives carrying their own history. The tradition treats it as something two people settle between them, with the Venus observances below as support; it is never read as a bar to marriage.
